title: Request Kitchen — Customer Insight Lab (notes & request compendium)
content:
Purpose
---
Capture a compact, useable compilation of raw asks, grouped hypotheses, and immediate small-scoped patches we can run against customer pain today. This is intentionally messy — think of it as the lab bench where CS and eng sketch quick probes.

One-line summary
---
Customers consistently surface three correlated friction clusters: (A) intermittent latency spikes on hosted endpoints with long-tail 95/99 latency behavior, (B) cost surprises around embedding-heavy workloads and token accounting, and (C) private deployment onboarding frictions (network config + KMS gaps). They want small guardrails and lightweight tooling to triage & mitigate before we roll bigger product work.

Raw highlights / representative quotes (redacted)
- "We see a handful of requests every day with one in 100 that takes 15–20s — kills our page flow." — fintech prod lead
- "Embeddings costs are unpredictable; caching behavior feels opaque after a week of heavy retrain/update cycles." — search team
- "Getting our on-prem instance to see KMS keys in our vault took 3 people 2 days — we need a checklist or better error surface." — platform engineer, regulated customer

Customer-asked items (clustered, short-ticket form)
1) Latency tail: introduce a 95/99 latency tag in the console per-route + per-model, with a quick diagnostic link that bundles a sample trace + request id list for ops handoff. (CS asked this so we can speed incident TTR.)
2) Embedding cost visibility: show per-indexing-run token/embedding unit breakdown, plus a simple TTL cache toggle in the dashboard for ephemeral indexes.
3) Private onboarding kit: one-click network checklist and sample iptables/cidr + KMS mapping examples for common enterprise vaults (HashiCorp, AWS KMS, Azure KeyVault).
4) Streaming resumes: small UX tweak — include a boolean to resume from last-ok token after transient network glitch (customer can opt-in).
5) Fallback model knob: UI slider to prefer cheaper compatible model under heavy load; expose estimated cost delta before enabling.

Quick prioritization (impact vs effort — heuristic)
- High impact / Low effort: 1) 95/99 latency tag + diagnostic bundle; 2) Embedding job cost breakdown in console.
- High impact / Medium effort: Fallback model knob with estimated cost delta; Streaming resume opt-in flag.
- Medium impact / High effort: Full private onboarding automation (lots of security/infra work).

Hypotheses (what we think is happening)
- Latency tail is driven by a mix of cold KV cache misses for long-lived chats and occasional slow kernel selection on specific model variants at high sequence lengths.
- Embedding cost surprises stem from: (a) repeated re-indexing without cache TTLs, (b) users not understanding dimension/encoding differences between model versions, (c) hidden per-call pre/post-processing tokenization overhead.
- Private onboarding friction = docs + sparse errors; customers often hit subtle TLS/cipher mismatches and KMS trust-chain errors that are opaque in our current logs.

Measurables / What success looks like
- TTR for latency incidents reduced from median 6h -> 90m when CS can attach diagnostic bundle (track 90-day window).
- Number of support tickets about embedding cost drops by 40% after adding per-run cost breakdown and TTL cache option (track 8 weeks post-launch).
- Average private onboarding time reduced from 48h -> 8h for median customers after publishing the onboarding kit + sample scripts.

Concrete quick experiments (MVPs to run in next 6 weeks)
A. Console flag + diagnostic bundle (2-week sprint)
- Deliverables: add 95/99 latency markers in per-route dashboard, button to collect last 100 request IDs + sample traces; small backend endpoint to snapshot traces into a ZIP for CS.
- Owners: Observability (Caroline) + CS (Aisha) + Eng (Ethan)
- Success metric: CS reports faster triage; pilot with 3 customers. Ticket: CSREQ-987

B. Embedding-run cost breakdown + TTL toggle (3-week sprint)
- Deliverables: surface tokens consumed per-job, estimated $ cost, toggle TTL for ephemeral caches; doc snippet explaining dimension choices.
- Owners: Product-optimize (Priya) + Backend (Jon)
- Success metric: decrease in embedding billing confusion threads; pilot with search customer.

C. Private onboarding kit (doc + sample scripts) (4-week content + vetting)
- Deliverables: network checklist, KMS mapping examples, troubleshooting checklist, sample terraform + iptables snippets, a short runbook for SREs.
- Owners: Private Deployments (Ethan) + Security (Caroline) + CS (Aisha)
- Success metric: anecdotal onboarding time reduction for first 5 customers who follow kit.

Small patches / quick wins (can be done as micro-PRs)
- Add clearer error codes and recommended next step strings for KMS failures (map common HSM/KMS error messages to >3 suggested actions).
- Add a console tooltip on embedding jobs that explains "what counts as a token here" with link to quick calculator.
- Expose a lightweight pre-flight network check runner (client-side script) customers can run and paste output to CS.

Open questions / risks
- Privacy: the diagnostic bundle must scrub PII by default. Need a clear scrub policy and opt-in for full raw traces. Who signs off? (Legal + Security).
- Cost estimation accuracy: per-run cost numbers are estimates; need to label them clearly and avoid disputes.
- Resource contention: if we expose fallback-model knob, we must ensure policy control to avoid noisy-neighbor impacts for Dedicated customers.

Next steps & owners (immediate week)
- Today: share this doc with Observability + Product-optimize + Private Deployments (Aisha).
- By Mon: Caroline to spin up a short spec for the diagnostic bundle (2 pager).
- By Wed: Priya to draft console UI copy for embedding-run breakdown and TTL toggle.
- Friday: quick sync with Legal about PII scrub requirements for trace bundles.

Notes to self (working artifacts to attach later)
- Example trace snippet (redacted) from cust-X on 2026-02-19 (to paste once scrubbed).
- Short recording of call with fintech customer (voice notes) — key quotes above.
- Pending: cost-est math from finance for embed units (reach out to Maya).

Appendix: quick mapping to existing backlog (avoid duplication)
- CSREQ-987 (new) — diagnostic bundle prototype
- RUNTIME-412 — kernel-selection perf fixes (related to latency tails)
- OPT-211 — embedding cost estimator (proposal, not yet scheduled)

If you read only one thing
---
Ship the 95/99 latency marker + diagnostic bundle and the embedding-run cost breakdown. Those two probes are small, unblock many CS threads, and give us real measurement to decide the heavier product investments.

End.
